note: Differences between the production recording and strict fireemu that are known and not aligned. Each entry names its rows and fields; a difference outside an entry is a MISMATCH. Header-level exclusions (strict-transport-security, x-robots-tag and the SDK-row headers) are in rows.mjs.

entries.reason: Production compresses these answers (gzip and br, ETag with a -br suffix) and strict does not: fireemu has no compression crate. The decoded body of every row is the file the corpus deployed; status, content type and the other headers of these rows are compared.
entries.authority: coordinator ruling 15 (2026-11-11); whether to add flate2 for gzip is put to the owner

entries.reason: Production answers an unmatched path with its own 21,376-byte Page Not Found page; the recording keeps only its digest, not its bytes, so strict answers with its own short page. Status, content type and the other headers of these rows are compared.
entries.authority: coordinator ruling 16 (2026-11-11); recording the page body is a To-Do for the next idp packet

entries.reason: Production answers a request for a parent directory with a 302 to an internal origin host (content-prodNN-firebasehosting-origin.googleapis.com) whose name differs from one request to the next, so no local answer can match it. Strict still refuses to leave the public directory.
The /__/firebase/<version>/*.js files are served by Google's CDN; a local fireemu has no network source for them and answers 503 offline.

Production's init.json holds the seven keys of the project's web app configuration; a local fireemu knows only the project id and a placeholder key, so the key set beyond apiKey and projectId (and the length of init.json and init.js) differ. Status and the other headers of these rows are compared.
The recorded requests are HEAD; the handler page production sends (462 bytes) was not recorded, so strict answers with a stand-in page of another length. Status and the other headers are compared.
